sentences.zh: 这个帝国吞并了萨非波斯的一部分、乌兹别克帝国的一部分以及莫卧儿印度的一部分，并首次建立了一个以喀布尔为中心、充满阿富汗人的帝国。

sentences.en: And the English, although the word Afghanistan is never used, the Kingdom of Kabul is the political phrase,
sentences.zh: 而英国人——尽管从未真正使用过“阿富汗”这个词，但“喀布尔王国”是当时的政治用语——

sentences.en: people do talk about, for the first time, Afghans.
sentences.zh: 人们确实第一次开始谈论“阿富汗人”了。

sentences.en: And so this is the beginning, in a sense, of the modern Afghan state.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这是现代阿富汗国家的开端。

sentences.en: And its borders are more or less those of Afghanistan, by default, because the Persians are where Persia is.
sentences.zh: 它的边界默认就是阿富汗现在的边界，因为波斯人就在波斯所在的地方。

sentences.zh: 莫卧儿印度现在随着锡克帝国和旁遮普的出现而告终，乌兹别克人也在阿姆河一带稳定了下来。

sentences.en: So you have this space in between, which of course is the title of Rory Stewart's book, which becomes Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 所以你有了中间这片空间，也就是罗里·斯图尔特那本书的标题，它成为了阿富汗。

sentences.en: And so are they consciously playing, I mean, are they consciously playing off the Russians and the British, because they're conscious of these two empires either side?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是有意在博弈吗？我是说，他们是否在有意识地利用俄国人和英国人，因为他们意识到这两大帝国就在两侧？

sentences.en: And half the story of it, which again has echoes today, is that the
sentences.zh: 而这故事的一半——今天依然有回响——就是

sentences.en: British fear of Russia creates the very nightmare that they fear.
sentences.zh: 英国对俄国的恐惧，反而制造了他们所恐惧的噩梦。

sentences.en: Because what happens is that following the sighting of Vickovich by Rawlinson, this meeting in the desert,
sentences.zh: 因为事情是这样的：在罗林森发现维科维奇之后，也就是在沙漠里的那次会面，

sentences.en: spies are sent off into Central Asia.
sentences.zh: 间谍被派往中亚。

sentences.en: One of these is Alexander Burns, who's also a great showman and a travel writer.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是亚历山大·伯恩斯，他也是一位伟大的表演家和游记作家。

sentences.en: And Alexander Burns has this wonderful moment when he travels up the Indus on a raft.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·伯恩斯有一个精彩的时刻，他乘木筏沿印度河而上。

sentences.en: And they have to have an excuse to get permission to go up the Indus.
sentences.zh: 他们必须找个借口才能获得沿印度河而上的许可。

sentences.en: So what they know is that Ranjit Singh, the Sikh ruler of Lahore, loves horses.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道，拉合尔的锡克统治者兰吉特·辛格非常喜欢马。

sentences.en: They decide to present him with four enormous English cart horses.
sentences.zh: 他们决定送给他四匹巨大的英国挽马。

sentences.en: And then just to add to the whole thing, they decide they're going to take an old carriage that used to belong to the Lord Mayor of London.
sentences.zh: 为了增加排场，他们还决定带上一辆曾经属于伦敦市长的旧马车。

sentences.en: And they stuff it full of geographers from the Admiralty, who are busy taking soundings on the depth of the Indus and the flow charts and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 他们把海军部的地理学家塞进马车里，这些人正忙着测量印度河的深度、绘制水流图等等。

sentences.en: So this is really quite a professional spying expedition.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一次相当专业的间谍考察。

sentences.en: It's heading up the Indus on a raft, being popped at, shots being popped at it by local tribesmen.
sentences.zh: 他们乘木筏沿印度河而上，还遭到当地部落民的射击。

sentences.en: With Burns sitting beside the Lord Mayor of London's coach and four English dray horses have been rather out of place.
sentences.zh: 伯恩斯坐在伦敦市长的马车旁，四匹英国挽马显得格格不入。

sentences.en: How has this not been made into a film?
sentences.zh: 这怎么还没被拍成电影？

sentences.en: And Burns, to fast forward, not only presents a whole body of espionage material to his paymaster, because he is a spy, but he also, as his cover, is the great geographer,
sentences.zh: 快进一下，伯恩斯不仅向他的雇主提交了大量间谍情报——因为他确实是个间谍——而且作为掩护，他还是位伟大的地理学家，

sentences.en: and he writes a three-volume account of his travels to Bacara, which becomes a bestseller.
sentences.zh: 他写了一部关于他前往布哈拉旅行的三卷本著作，成为了畅销书。

sentences.en: He's received by Queen Victoria, who thinks he's very charming.
sentences.zh: 他受到了维多利亚女王的接见，女王觉得他非常有魅力。

sentences.en: He gets not only the gold medal of the
sentences.zh: 他不仅获得了伦敦

sentences.en: Royal Geographical Society in London, but he also gets its French equivalent.
sentences.zh: 皇家地理学会的金质奖章，还获得了法国同行的奖章。

sentences.en: His book is translated to French, and of course, the Russians read it.
sentences.zh: 他的书被翻译成法文，当然，俄国人也读了。

sentences.en: And the Russians, who do not have spies in Bacara, then send Vickovich to spy it out.
sentences.zh: 而那些在布哈拉没有间谍的俄国人，随后派出了维科维奇去刺探情况。

sentences.en: And Vickovich successfully rolls up Alexander Byrne's espionage network that he's set up in Bacara.
sentences.zh: 维科维奇成功地摧毁了亚历山大·伯恩斯在布哈拉建立的间谍网。

sentences.en: I mean, so it's actually no more than a couple of carpet dealers, but already everyone knows they're working for the British.
sentences.zh: 我是说，其实那不过是几个地毯商，但大家早就知道他们是在为英国人工作。

sentences.en: But basically, the key is don't write a book.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，关键是别写书。

sentences.en: Don't tell everyone what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 别告诉所有人你在做什么。

sentences.en: I mean, it's mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so the British managed to create a paranoia in the Russians.
sentences.zh: 总之，英国人成功地在俄国人心中制造了偏执。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a very generalised fear that the Russians definitely are moving south.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当时确实有一种普遍的恐惧，认为俄国人肯定在向南推进。

sentences.en: But no, the Russians do not specifically have their eyes on Afghanistan, and certainly up to this point, other than a brief moment when, again, another wonderful Raft story.

sentences.en: There's the famous moment of Tilsit, when Alexander, the Tsar of Russia, and Napoleon meet on a barge and plan to obey India together in 1810.
sentences.zh: 那是著名的提尔西特时刻，1810年，俄国沙皇亚历山大和拿破仑在一艘驳船上会面，计划共同征服印度。

sentences.en: 1812 is the retreat.
sentences.zh: 1812年是撤退。

sentences.en: So 1809, 1812, War and Peace opens before Tilsit.
sentences.zh: 所以1809年、1812年，《战争与和平》开篇就在提尔西特之前。

sentences.en: That's book one of War and Peace.
sentences.zh: 那是《战争与和平》的第一卷。

sentences.en: Today we always read it as War and Peace, but it's actually three volumes before Tilsit as well.
sentences.zh: 今天我们总是把它读作《战争与和平》，但实际上在提尔西特之前还有三卷。

sentences.en: And the story goes, again, allegedly, but I don't know whether it's true, that there is a British spy under the Raft.
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，当然，据说是这样，我不知道是不是真的，说木筏下面藏着一个英国间谍。

sentences.en: I hope it's true.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是真的。

sentences.en: Peter Hopkirk has this in his book, Other People Have Fibbled It, but I certainly want to believe it.
sentences.zh: 彼得·霍普柯克在他的书里提到了这一点，虽然别人对此表示怀疑，但我确实想相信它。

sentences.en: And definitely there are plans that Napoleon hatch is very far-fetched and bonkers to invade India.

sentences.zh: 现在沙·舒贾流亡到了英属印度，被当作英国的傀儡储备起来，英国人想用的时候随时可以让他复辟。

sentences.zh: 多斯特·穆罕默德，他的敌人，现在统治着阿富汗。

sentences.zh: 这是真的吗，威利？

sentences.zh: 我可以打断你吗？

sentences.zh: 我读到多斯特·穆罕默德有16个妻子、27个儿子和25个女儿，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Wow.

sentences.zh: 那是个大家庭聚会。

sentences.zh: 你可以想象，当你前面有17个哥哥时，要成为统治继承人……

sentences.zh: 他们对这个迷人年轻人的成功嫉妒得发狂。

sentences.zh: 而此时，东印度公司甚至连阿富汗的地图都没有。

sentences.zh: 他们必须穿过锡克人的旁遮普。

sentences.zh: 旁遮普雄狮兰吉特·辛格拥有一支由前拿破仑将军训练出来的极其出色的军队。

sentences.en: He has fantastic cannon, which anyone who's in London can see, because they're now lined up on the lawns of Chelsea Hospital.
sentences.zh: 他有很棒的加农炮，任何在伦敦的人都能看到，因为它们现在排列在切尔西医院的草坪上。

sentences.en: If you go into Chelsea, you can see all these fantastic state-of-the-art Sikh cannon with all Ranjit Singh's insignia on them.
sentences.zh: 如果你去切尔西，你可以看到所有这些最先进的锡克加农炮，上面还有兰吉特·辛格的徽章。

sentences.zh: 于是军队出发了。

sentences.zh: 2万名士兵离开了旁遮普的费罗兹普尔。

sentences.zh: 随行的是这些奇特的随军家属。

sentences.zh: 一位将军有26头骆驼来运送他的装备和酒吧。

sentences.zh: 有五头骆驼专门用来运送军队的雪茄供应。

sentences.zh: 一头骆驼什么都不带。

sentences.zh: 还有一头骆驼完全是用来运送古龙水的。

sentences.zh: 这让你为身为英国人感到自豪。

sentences.zh: 大量的印度兵因为没有水而死亡，伤亡惨重。

sentences.zh: 他们让你占领城市，然后一切就从游击活动开始了。

sentences.zh: 而这正是所发生的一切。

sentences.zh: 但有一个冬天，英国人在喀布尔搞起了业余戏剧表演。

sentences.zh: 想必钢琴在那里非常有用。

sentences.en: In the meantime, the man put in charge of this, a guy called McNaughton, who is an Orientalist, who goes, at one point, certainly, he's on the top of an elephant

sentences.zh: 当他进入喀布尔时，正在翻译阿拉伯语的《一千零一夜》。

sentences.en: And he revived his mission.
sentences.zh: 他恢复了他的使命。

sentences.zh: 而戴着蓝色眼镜的麦克诺顿，也像其他人一样，讨厌亚历山大·伯恩斯。

sentences.en: And there's dancing.

sentences.zh: 所以他是罗比·伯恩斯的堂兄，尽管他的名字拼写完全不同。

sentences.en: And there's reels and there's haggises in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 喀布尔还有苏格兰圆舞和哈吉斯肉馅羊肚。

sentences.en: But with nothing better to do, he gets back again, and he starts seducing the wives of the Afghan warlords.
sentences.zh: 但由于无事可做，他又重操旧业，开始勾引阿富汗军阀的妻子们。

sentences.zh: 当然，这是一件非常糟糕的事情。

sentences.zh: 如果你在阿富汗，千万不要和任何军阀的妻子睡觉。

sentences.zh: 而这正是引发叛乱的直接原因。

sentences.en: He takes the mistress of one of the tribal leaders called Abdullah Khan Achaqzai.
sentences.zh: 他带走了部落首领之一阿卜杜拉·汗·阿查克扎伊的情妇。

sentences.en: And according to one of the Afghan epic poems, which my friend Bruce Whannell translated to me about this,
sentences.zh: 根据我朋友布鲁斯·惠内尔为我翻译的一首关于此事的阿富汗史诗，

sentences.zh: 有一段话是阿卜杜拉·汗·阿查克扎伊召集他的部落成员说：英国人已经骑着欲望的驴子冲进了愚蠢的田野。

sentences.en: This will cost me my favorite time in the whole book.
sentences.zh: 这会让我付出整本书中最喜欢的时光。

sentences.zh: 我们都必须避免骑着欲望的驴子冲进愚蠢的田野。

sentences.zh: 好吧，威利，我认为这是一个快速休息的完美节点。

sentences.zh: 她们中有些人以美貌著称，有些人以政治敏锐度著称，还有些人以卖橙子的本领著称。

sentences.zh: 我们一直在骑着欲望的驴子冲进愚蠢的田野，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.zh: 我预见前方有灾难。

sentences.zh: 威廉·达尔林普尔，我说得对吗？

sentences.en: You are exactly right,
sentences.zh: 你完全正确，

sentences.zh: 唐纳德·扎布鲁克。

sentences.zh: 这正是所发生的事情。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: the Afghan tribes rise up, and quite a lot of the tribes had been very happy to support Shah Tujim, and were pleased to see him back,
sentences.zh: 阿富汗部落起义了，虽然很多部落曾很高兴支持舒贾·沙，也很高兴看到他回来，

sentences.en: but none of them like this British occupation force.
sentences.zh: 但他们都不喜欢这支英国占领军。

sentences.en: And the East India Company army has behaved as it would have done in Bengal.
sentences.zh: 东印度公司的军队表现得就像他们在孟加拉时一样。

sentences.en: They've laid out, first of all, their tents, then afterwards the tents are replaced by wooden, and then a few brick structures, or stone structures,
sentences.zh: 他们首先搭起了帐篷，后来帐篷被木制结构取代，然后是一些砖石结构，

sentences.en: on the plains outside Kabul, as if it was the plains of Bengal.
sentences.zh: 在喀布尔郊外的平原上，就好像那是孟加拉的平原一样。

sentences.en: Apparently, admitting to notice that every single one of these tents is overlooked by mountains immediately on top, and perfect sniper territory.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们没注意到每一个帐篷都被头顶上的山脉俯瞰着，那是完美的狙击阵地。

sentences.en: And they're too busy fox hunting and doing Scots reels, and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 他们太忙于猎狐和跳苏格兰圆舞，以及所有其他这些事情了。

sentences.en: So that when the uprising breaks out,
sentences.zh: 所以当起义爆发时，

sentences.en: very quickly, the insurgents steal some East India Company cannon, pull it onto the hills around the camp, and start bombarding it.
sentences.zh: 叛军很快就偷走了一些东印度公司的火炮，拉到营地周围的山上，开始轰炸营地。

sentences.en: And it's a completely indefensible position.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全无法防御的位置。

sentences.en: And then, as chance to have it, because this uprising was not particularly planned, it was started by Abdullah Khan Atchak's eye,

sentences.zh: 因为他的女朋友跑到了亚历山大·伯恩斯的家里。

sentences.en: Just a quick question about the army,
sentences.zh: 关于军队的一个小问题，

sentences.en: Willie, that occurs to me.
sentences.zh: 威利，我突然想到了。

sentences.en: You described them as East India Company cannon.
sentences.zh: 你把它们描述为东印度公司的火炮。

sentences.en: So is this definitely an East India Company expedition rather than a British national expedition?
sentences.zh: 那么这绝对是东印度公司的远征，而不是英国国家的远征吗？

sentences.en: So when we were talking about the anarchy, and particularly battles like Plassey, on the last time I came to the show, it's a very black and white thing,
sentences.zh: 当我们上次在节目中谈论无政府状态，特别是像普拉西战役这样的战斗时，那是非常黑白分明的事情，

sentences.en: because the company had 200,000 sepoids, which were the force, which invaded the whole of India.
sentences.zh: 因为公司拥有20万名土兵，这就是入侵整个印度的力量。

sentences.en: But in this case, there are now a mixture of regiments of the line, in other words, its regular British army fighting alongside East India Company seapoints.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，现在混合了正规军团，换句话说，是正规英国军队与东印度公司土兵并肩作战。

sentences.en: So the great mass of troops are East India Company seapoints, but I think there are at least two regiments of a regular British army.
sentences.zh: 所以大部分军队是东印度公司的土兵，但我认为至少有两个正规英国陆军团。

sentences.en: So it's a mix.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个混合体。

sentences.en: So this is reflecting the position of the East India Company, which by the 1840s has become much more of what I suppose today we would call a public-private punch.
sentences.zh: 这反映了东印度公司的地位，到19世纪40年代，它已经变得更像我们今天所说的公私合营企业。

sentences.en: What started off as the ultimate libertarian trading company with no government links at all, other than a charter to start it, has now become 50% owned by the British government,
sentences.zh: 最初作为一个终极的自由贸易公司，除了成立时的特许状外，与政府没有任何联系，现在已经有50%由英国政府拥有，

sentences.en: and by 1840 has actually been forbidden to, has lost its monopoly to trade.
sentences.zh: 到1840年，它实际上已被禁止，失去了贸易垄断权。

sentences.en: And so it's looking much more like a semi-governmental organization than the early days of Clive and Hastings.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来更像是一个半政府组织，而不是克莱夫和黑斯廷斯早期的样子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The more pioneering thing.
sentences.zh: 更具开创性的事情。

sentences.en: But still, the fact remains, almost all the troops are Indian sepoys born in India, the some Nepalis and some Gurkhas.
sentences.zh: 但事实仍然是，几乎所有的士兵都是在印度出生的印度土兵，还有一些尼泊尔人和廓尔喀人。

sentences.en: But, and then there's a regiment of Skinner's Horse, for example, which is, you know, led by Anglo-Indians, the Skinner family.
sentences.zh: 但是，还有一个斯金纳骑兵团，例如，是由英裔印度人斯金纳家族领导的。

sentences.en: But there are several regiments of the line.
sentences.zh: 但也有几个正规军团。

sentences.en: And there's a snobbery of hierarchy here.
sentences.zh: 这里存在一种等级势利。

sentences.en: And the regiments of the line of the British army consider themselves superior to the East India Company.
sentences.zh: 英国陆军的正规军团认为自己比东印度公司优越。

sentences.en: The East India Company, however, speak Urdu and Hindi and feel that they're much superior to the British army.
sentences.zh: 然而，东印度公司的人会说乌尔都语和印地语，觉得他们比英国陆军优越得多。

sentences.en: We don't know what's going on locally.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道当地发生了什么。

sentences.en: So there's lots of rivalry going on.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多竞争在进行。

sentences.zh: 这反映在对起义的反应上。

sentences.en: Because the Elphinstone, William Elphinstone, who is the very dim cousin of the brilliant Mount Stewart Elphinstone,
sentences.zh: 因为埃尔芬斯通，威廉·埃尔芬斯通，他是杰出的蒙特斯图尔特·埃尔芬斯通那个非常迟钝的堂兄，
zh_words: 蒙特斯图尔特·埃尔芬斯通

sentences.en: who is a gouty veteran of Waterloo who hasn't seen action since 1815.
sentences.zh: 他是一位患有痛风的滑铁卢老兵，自1815年以来就没有参加过战斗。

sentences.en: We're now talking 1842, January.
sentences.zh: 我们现在谈论的是1842年1月。

sentences.en: And his deputy, who's a man called Shelton,
sentences.zh: 而他的副手，一个叫谢尔顿的人，

sentences.en: and he are on non-speaks.
sentences.zh: 他们两人互不说话。

sentences.en: They are massive divisions.
sentences.zh: 他们之间存在巨大的分歧。

sentences.en: And it's a complete fiasco.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一场惨败。

sentences.en: Not only are the companies defeated in battle on the few occasions they do ride out and try and take on the insurgents in the hills around the country.
sentences.zh: 公司军队不仅在他们偶尔出击试图在乡村周围的山丘上对付叛军时在战斗中失败，

sentences.en: They are running out of food.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的食物也快吃完了。

sentences.en: Lady Sale has now had to burn her grand piano for firewood because they've run out of heating material.
sentences.zh: 赛尔夫人现在不得不烧掉她的三角钢琴来取暖，因为他们已经没有取暖材料了。

sentences.en: They've eaten the foxhounds by the stage.
sentences.zh: 到这个阶段，他们已经吃掉了猎狐犬。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very bad form.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But the cricket bats are all right.
sentences.zh: 但板球拍还好。

sentences.en: Please tell me the cricket bats are okay.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我板球拍没事。

sentences.en: I think the cricket bats, I suspect, would also have been burnt.
sentences.zh: 我想板球拍，我怀疑，也已经被烧掉了。

sentences.en: You know things are getting bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道情况正在变得糟糕。

sentences.en: There's a primary source evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 有原始资料证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: Anyway, there's obviously no option but to retreat.
sentences.zh: 总之，显然除了撤退别无选择。

sentences.en: And it's now January 1842.
sentences.zh: 现在是1842年1月。

sentences.en: And the Afghans seem to be dragging their feet a little during negotiations.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人在谈判期间似乎有点拖延。

sentences.en: And people are mystified by this because they think, you know, they probably want to get rid of us as much as we want to get out of here.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到困惑，因为他们认为，你知道，他们可能和我们想离开这里一样，想摆脱我们。

sentences.en: And it drags on for two or three weeks.
sentences.zh: 这拖延了两三个星期。

sentences.en: Finally, the moment comes January when they set off into the snow.
sentences.zh: 终于，1月份的时刻到了，他们出发进入雪地。

sentences.en: And everyone knows this is not looking good.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这看起来不妙。

sentences.en: The past is, are anyway, almost entirely blocked.
sentences.zh: 山口无论如何几乎完全被封锁了。

sentences.en: No one moves armies around Central Asia in the middle of winter.
sentences.zh: 没有人会在隆冬时节在亚洲中部调动军队。

sentences.en: Because you can, you know, freeze in seconds outside your tent.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以在帐篷外几秒钟内冻僵。

sentences.en: And what, of course, has happened is the Afghans prepared a whole series of barricades and ambushes.
sentences.zh: 当然，发生的事情是阿富汗人准备了一系列路障和伏击。

sentences.en: And they're just waiting for them.
sentences.zh: 他们就在那里等着他们。

sentences.en: And within a few hours of setting off from the cantoonement, not only have tax begun on the column, but the cantoonement has been burnt down and looted.
sentences.zh: 从营地出发后的几个小时内，不仅纵队开始受到攻击，而且营地也被烧毁和洗劫了。

sentences.en: Rather like some of the scenes seen in Kabul this weekend of looting.
sentences.zh: 就像这个周末在喀布尔看到的抢劫场景一样。

sentences.en: And the people run.
sentences.zh: 人们在奔跑。

sentences.en: Oh, no, exactly what happened to Bamiya when it was deserted a month ago.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，这正是一个月前巴米扬被遗弃时发生的事情。

sentences.en: Exactly what happened at Bagram Air Base when the Americans left it two months ago.
sentences.zh: 这正是两个月前美国人离开巴格拉姆空军基地时发生的事情。

sentences.en: The locals just ran in and looted it.
sentences.zh: 当地人跑进去洗劫了它。

sentences.en: It's exactly what happens in the British cantoonement in January 1842.
sentences.zh: 这正是1842年1月英国营地发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the first night, the British are stuck in the snow, having snipers firing at them,
sentences.zh: 所以第一天晚上，英国人被困在雪地里，有狙击手向他们开火，

sentences.en: and they can see behind them the flames of the cantoonement, the light of the cantoonement, flickering fires.
sentences.zh: 他们可以看到身后营地的火焰，营地的光亮，闪烁的火光。

sentences.en: And they know there's no retreat.
sentences.zh: 他们知道没有退路了。

sentences.en: They can't go back.
sentences.zh: 他们无法回头。

sentences.en: But it's five days march to Jolanda.
sentences.zh: 但到贾拉拉巴德还有五天的路程。

sentences.en: And what I remember from Flashman is that Elphinstone gets shot in the buttocks, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我从《闪电侠》中记得埃尔芬斯通屁股中弹了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's so much with Flashman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那更多是《闪电侠》里的内容。

sentences.en: There's an awful lot which is historically accurate.
sentences.zh: 有很多内容在历史上是准确的。

sentences.en: But a certain amount of light...
sentences.zh: 但一定程度的艺术加工……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK, so that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以那没发生。

sentences.en: That's terrible.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: The one fact I remember isn't true.
sentences.zh: 我记得的唯一一个事实竟然不是真的。

sentences.en: Elphinstone is definitely wounded.
sentences.zh: 埃尔芬斯通确实受伤了。

sentences.en: But in the sources I've read, buttocks are not...
sentences.zh: 但在我读过的资料中，屁股并没有……

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But yes, Elfie Bay, as he's called, is wounded, has a stroke, I think, probably, in the middle of all this horror.
sentences.zh: 但是是的，埃尔菲贝，正如他被称呼的那样，受伤了，我想在所有这些恐怖之中，他可能中风了。

sentences.en: And day by day, the number of survivors goes down from 20,000 to 10,000 to 5,000 to 2,000.
sentences.zh: 日复一日，幸存者人数从2万减少到1万，再到5千，再到2千。

sentences.en: There's a terrible moment at a place called Jigdulik, where the holly hedge is erected in their path.
sentences.zh: 在吉格达利克有一个可怕的时刻，冬青树篱被竖立在他们的路上。

sentences.en: And the cavalry, which so far have been marching out fairly easily, can't get over this.
sentences.zh: 而到目前为止行军还算顺利的骑兵无法越过这个障碍。

sentences.en: And they're shot down, and people are crawling over it.
sentences.zh: 他们被射杀，人们在上面爬行。

sentences.en: And several hundred die on this hedge, unable to cross this barrier that's erected in their way.
sentences.zh: 几百人死在了这道树篱上，无法跨越这道横亘在他们面前的障碍。

sentences.en: And finally, there's a bunch of lancers making the last stretch, and the 51st foot, who form themselves into a square on the hill of Gundamuk,
sentences.zh: 最后，还有一群枪骑兵在做最后的冲刺，而第51步兵团在冈达马克山上结成了方阵，

sentences.en: fight until their ammunition is exhausted, and then form a bayonet line.
sentences.zh: 他们战斗到弹尽粮绝，然后组成了刺刀阵线。

sentences.en: There's a very famous painting of this, isn't there, Willie?
sentences.zh: 有一幅关于此事的名画，不是吗，威利？

sentences.en: Famous painting, exactly.
sentences.zh: 名画，确实如此。

sentences.en: And they fight until their last bullet.
sentences.zh: 他们战斗到最后一颗子弹。

sentences.en: They form a bayonet war.
sentences.zh: 他们展开了刺刀战。

sentences.en: But the Afghans realize there's no need to charge bayonets.
sentences.zh: 但阿富汗人意识到没必要进行刺刀冲锋。

sentences.en: They just pull back.
sentences.zh: 他们只是撤退。

sentences.en: And one of the features of the war is that the Afghans have this very old-fashioned Mughal jazale, which is a hunting rifle that Shah Jahan could be seen using to hunt deer.
sentences.zh: 这场战争的一个特点是，阿富汗人拥有这种非常老式的莫卧儿火绳枪，这是一种沙贾汗曾用来猎鹿的猎枪。

sentences.en: And it's a big, heavy, unwieldy thing.
sentences.zh: 它又大、又重、又笨重。

sentences.en: But it has a very long barrel and is accurate over a distance of about half a mile, while the Brambest musket fires only 300 yards.
sentences.zh: 但它枪管很长，在半英里左右的距离内很精准，而布朗贝斯滑膛枪只能射击300码。

sentences.en: So they realize there's no need to take these guys on shoulder to shoulder.
sentences.zh: 所以他们意识到没必要和这些人肩并肩地肉搏。

sentences.en: They just pull back and shoot from a distance.
sentences.zh: 他们只是撤退并从远处射击。

sentences.en: And every last man is killed, except for one guy who has wrapped himself in the colors.
sentences.zh: 最后每个人都被杀了，除了一个人，他把自己裹在军旗里。

sentences.en: And he's taken hostage because they think he must be worth something because he's got such fancy colored clothes on.
sentences.zh: 他被俘虏了，因为他们认为他一定很有价值，因为他穿着如此华丽的彩色衣服。

sentences.en: And that is a guy called Thomas Souter.
sentences.zh: 那个人叫托马斯·苏特。

sentences.en: And the first British camp in Helmand was called Camp Souter, after his memory.
sentences.zh: 赫尔曼省的第一个英国营地就以他的名字命名为苏特营地，以纪念他。

sentences.en: Anyway, this leaves some lancers who are cut down one by one by the last of the cavalry, until only Dr. Brydon is left on his nag.
sentences.zh: 总之，这留下了一些被最后的骑兵一个接一个砍倒的枪骑兵，直到只剩下布莱登医生骑着他的小马。

sentences.en: And the reason Dr. Brydon survives is he has a copy of Blackwood's magazine.
sentences.zh: 布莱登医生幸存下来的原因是，他有一本《布莱克伍德杂志》。

sentences.en: He's a reader.
sentences.zh: 他是个读书人。

sentences.en: He would definitely have subscribed to the rest of his history if he was around today.
sentences.zh: 如果他活在今天，他肯定会订阅他余下的历史。

sentences.en: And he has a copy of Blackwood's magazine in his forage cap so that when these two Afghan horsemen come from him,
sentences.zh: 他的草帽里塞着一本《布莱克伍德杂志》，所以当这两个阿富汗骑兵冲向他时，

sentences.en: one of them shoots a pistol which misfires, and then he hacks at him with a sword.
sentences.zh: 其中一个开了一枪，结果哑火了，然后他用剑砍向他。

sentences.en: But it goes into Blackwood's magazine, which is sitting in his hat, because he seemingly wanted to read in the evening.
sentences.zh: 但剑砍进了他帽子里的《布莱克伍德杂志》，因为他似乎想在晚上阅读。

sentences.en: And doesn't pierce his skull.
sentences.zh: 所以没有刺穿他的头骨。

sentences.en: And he alone, of the British troops, makes it through to Jalalabad.
sentences.zh: 他是英军中唯一一个成功到达贾拉拉巴德的人。

sentences.en: Did Blackwood use that as a kind of advertising slogan?
sentences.zh: 布莱克伍德把这当作一种广告口号了吗？

sentences.en: Should have done.
sentences.zh: 本该如此。

sentences.en: Read Blackwood's.
sentences.zh: 读《布莱克伍德》。

sentences.en: It'll keep you alive.
sentences.zh: 它能保住你的命。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing the TLS would do, or London Review of Books or something.
sentences.zh: 这正是《泰晤士报文学增刊》或《伦敦书评》之类会做的事。

sentences.en: Contrary to the myth, he's not the only survivor.
sentences.zh: 与神话相反，他并不是唯一的幸存者。

sentences.en: He's not even the only white survivor.
sentences.zh: 他甚至不是唯一的白人幸存者。

sentences.en: Several other troops straggling after him.
sentences.zh: 还有其他几名士兵在他之后零星地逃了出来。

sentences.en: Bizarrely, a Greek shopkeeper who'd been running this sort of kebab shop at the contoonement, has hidden in a cave and comes in with a bottle of Uzu a week later.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，一个在营地经营烤肉店的希腊店主躲在山洞里，一周后带着一瓶乌佐酒出现了。

sentences.en: And there's a whole bunch of Nepali Gurkhas who have just gone up some valleys and are completely happy with the temperature and are completely used to surviving.
sentences.zh: 还有一大群尼泊尔廓尔喀人，他们只是走进了山谷，对气温完全适应，并且完全习惯了生存。

sentences.en: And so the Gurkhas sort of reappear about a week later in perfect order with their medal shining and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 所以廓尔喀人大约一周后以完美的秩序重新出现，勋章闪闪发光，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then some of the Hindu sepoys turn up a year and a half later at the Kummela in Hardwa, having walked all the way home.
sentences.zh: 然后一些印度土兵在一年半后出现在哈里瓦的昆梅拉节上，他们一路走回了家。

sentences.en: So he's not, in fact, the only survivor.
sentences.zh: 所以事实上，他并不是唯一的幸存者。

sentences.en: So two people, what their fits.
sentences.zh: 所以两个人，他们的合适之处。

sentences.en: So Lady Sale.
sentences.zh: 还有萨尔夫人。

sentences.en: Lady Sale, along with all the other ladies or several of the other ladies, not all of them, many are killed.
sentences.zh: 萨尔夫人，连同其他所有女士或几位其他女士，并非全部，许多人被杀了。

sentences.en: But Lady Sale, along with several others, have taken hostage.
sentences.zh: 但萨尔夫人和其他几个人被俘虏了。

sentences.en: And then there's protracted hostage negotiations.
sentences.zh: 然后是旷日持久的人质谈判。

sentences.en: And basically, at the end of the day, there's a swap.
sentences.zh: 基本上，归根结底，是一次交换。

sentences.en: Dos Mohamed, who had been captured, or rather given himself up, had been kept in some, in the British hill station of Missouri in the Himalayas.
sentences.zh: 多斯特·穆罕默德，他曾被俘，或者说是自首了，一直被关在喜马拉雅山脉的英国山地车站穆索里。

sentences.en: Dos Mohamed is brought back.
sentences.zh: 多斯特·穆罕默德被带了回来。

sentences.en: And the man negotiating is Dos Mohamed's son, Akbar Khan, who is a young, handsome sort of movie hero type,
sentences.zh: 负责谈判的人是多斯特·穆罕默德的儿子阿克巴尔·汗，他是一个年轻、英俊的电影英雄类型的人，

sentences.en: who's led this resistance and planned the holly hedge at Jigdalic and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 他领导了这次抵抗，并策划了贾格达拉克的树篱等等。

sentences.en: And Dos Mohamed is brought home.
sentences.zh: 多斯特·穆罕默德被带回家了。

sentences.en: He makes an agreement with the British that he will not allow the Russians in.
sentences.zh: 他与英国人达成协议，他不会让俄国人进来。

sentences.en: And otherwise, he's allowed to come back unmolested.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他被允许不受干扰地回来。

sentences.en: And you end up, and Lady Sale and the others are swapped for him.
sentences.zh: 最后，萨尔夫人和其他人被换回了他。

sentences.en: And they haven't been molested.
sentences.zh: 他们没有受到骚扰。

sentences.en: There are several other...
sentences.zh: 还有其他几个人……

sentences.en: They've been looked after well, have they?
sentences.zh: 他们被照顾得很好，是吗？

sentences.en: Or have they fared in captivity?
sentences.zh: 还是他们在囚禁中过得怎么样？

sentences.en: A hundred and a hundred years who kept very well, including my direct forebear, Colin McKenzie, who's dressed up in Afghan dress, making a great sort of...
sentences.zh: 一百年又一百年，他们过得很好，包括我的直系祖先科林·麦肯齐，他穿着阿富汗服装，表现得非常……

sentences.en: He has lots of self-portraits painted when he gets home in Afghan dress, all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他回家后画了很多穿着阿富汗服装的自画像，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And these...
sentences.zh: 而这些……

sentences.en: The war ends exactly as this war has ended, with the government, which was in power before all this, coming back into power.
sentences.zh: 战争结束的方式与这场战争结束的方式完全一样，在此之前掌权的政府又重新掌权了。

sentences.en: And because no one can threaten it anymore because of the enormous prestige it's won, defeating imperial power,
sentences.zh: 而且因为没有人能再威胁它，因为它在击败帝国力量后赢得了巨大的声望，

sentences.en: Dos Mohamed then stays in power for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 多斯特·穆罕默德此后余生一直掌权。

sentences.en: And he has a very grand tomb, which I've seen in the Garzagar in Herat, one of the most beautiful Sufi shrines in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他有一座非常宏伟的陵墓，我在赫拉特的加扎加尔见过，是阿富汗最美丽的苏菲派圣地之一。

sentences.en: And, Willie, what about Shah Shuja?
sentences.zh: 那么，威利，沙舒贾怎么样？

sentences.en: Shah Shuja.
sentences.zh: 沙舒贾。

sentences.en: So Shah Shuja, who is the hero of my book, Return of the King, the King in question, is Shah Shuja.
sentences.zh: 所以沙舒贾，也就是我那本书《国王归来》中的英雄，那位国王，就是沙舒贾。

sentences.en: Shah Shuja is a very attractive character.
sentences.zh: 沙舒贾是一个非常有吸引力的人物。

sentences.en: He is a poet.
sentences.zh: 他是一位诗人。

sentences.en: He is...
He keeps his nerve when the uprising breaks out in Kabul and when the British flee and desert him.
sentences.zh: 当喀布尔爆发起义，英国人逃跑并抛弃他时，他保持了冷静。

sentences.en: He's holed up in the Bala Hussar, having defended it very admirably.
sentences.zh: 他躲在巴拉希萨尔城堡里，防守得非常出色。

sentences.en: He's an extremely brave man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极其勇敢的人。

sentences.en: His floor is he's too grand.
sentences.zh: 他的缺点是他太讲排场了。

sentences.en: He doesn't...
sentences.zh: 他没有……

sentences.en: He makes everybody stand in his derbars, which was the Mughal style, and his mother is Mughal.
sentences.zh: 他让所有人都站在他的朝廷里，这是莫卧儿风格，而他的母亲是莫卧儿人。

sentences.en: But it's not the manner the Afghans used to.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是阿富汗人习惯的方式。

sentences.en: They're used to sitting down on the carpet altogether in a tribal jirga.
sentences.zh: 他们习惯在部落支尔格会议上一起坐在地毯上。

sentences.en: And this egalitarian mode is what makes Dos Mohamed say successful.
sentences.zh: 而这种平等主义模式正是多斯特·穆罕默德成功的原因。

sentences.en: He doesn't play grand.
sentences.zh: 他不摆架子。

sentences.en: He entertains and charms all his tribesmen.
sentences.zh: 他招待并吸引了他所有的部落成员。

sentences.en: And this is one of the many parallels, if we can move on to parallels, with the president.
sentences.zh: 这是许多相似之处之一，如果我们能谈谈相似之处，与总统的相似之处。

sentences.en: Because...
sentences.zh: 因为……

sentences.en: But just before that, what happens to Shah Shuja?
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，沙舒贾发生了什么？

sentences.en: Shah Shuja survives all this.
sentences.zh: 沙舒贾在这一切中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: The British cut up.
sentences.zh: 英国人撤走了。

sentences.en: The deals are done.
sentences.zh: 交易达成了。

sentences.en: And Shah Shuja, in the end, is killed by a godson who wants to get in with Dos Mohamed.
sentences.zh: 最后，沙舒贾被一个想讨好多斯特·穆罕默德的教子杀死了。

sentences.en: But for that, he may well have survived the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 如果不是那样，他很可能在整件事中幸存下来。

sentences.en: But he has slighted a godson who feels he hasn't been given promotion or something.
sentences.zh: 但他怠慢了一个教子，那个教子觉得他没有得到晋升之类的。

sentences.en: So it's a small, petty internal feud.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场小小的、琐碎的内部争斗。

sentences.en: So it's rudeness that does it.
sentences.zh: 所以是粗鲁导致了这一切。

sentences.en: And sorry, I interrupted you when you were talking about the parallels, because that is a great parallel, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 抱歉，你谈论相似之处时我打断了你，因为那是一个很好的相似之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because there is a huge premium in Afghanistan still on basic climate.
sentences.zh: 因为在阿富汗，基本的礼貌仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: And this was one of the great qualities of Hamid Karzai, who would make every Afghan, particularly any tribal elder who'd come in from the countryside,
sentences.zh: 这是哈米德·卡尔扎伊的伟大品质之一，他会让每个阿富汗人，特别是任何从乡下进城的部落长老，

sentences.en: he would give them time, he would talk to them, he would...
sentences.zh: 他会给他们时间，他会和他们交谈，他会……

sentences.en: So he was the first president of...
sentences.zh: 所以他是第一任总统……

sentences.en: Stalled in what, 2002?
sentences.zh: 停滞在什么，2002年？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the important point, as far as, again, this war is concerned that we're talking about, is he is the direct descendant of Shah Shuja.
sentences.zh: 但就我们正在谈论的这场战争而言，重要的一点是，他是沙舒贾的直系后裔。

sentences.en: He is the head of the Pudulzai tribe.
sentences.zh: 他是波帕尔扎伊部落的首领。

sentences.en: We basically put the same guy in twice.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上两次扶持了同一个人。

sentences.en: Karzai is a slightly nicer version of Shah Shuja.
sentences.zh: 卡尔扎伊是沙舒贾的一个稍微好一点的版本。

sentences.en: And Karzai did actually an incredible job, charming everyone.
sentences.zh: 卡尔扎伊确实做得非常出色，吸引了每个人。

sentences.en: And his replacement, Ashraf Ghani, who, incidentally, is a good friend, was very kind to me,
sentences.zh: 而他的继任者阿什拉夫·加尼，顺便说一句，他是我的好朋友，对我非常友善，

sentences.en: is the man that helped me find a lot of the sources from the book when he was head of the history department and chancellor of Kabul University.
sentences.zh: 当他担任历史系主任和喀布尔大学校长时，他帮助我找到了书中许多资料。

sentences.en: Ashraf was incredibly rude to people.
sentences.zh: 阿什拉夫对人非常粗鲁。

sentences.en: He was very grand.
sentences.zh: 他非常讲排场。

sentences.en: He had worked for the World Bank, taught at Columbia.
sentences.zh: 他曾在世界银行工作，在哥伦比亚大学教书。

sentences.en: He didn't have time for fools.
sentences.zh: 他没有时间应付傻瓜。

sentences.en: He was a very successful university professor and World Bank technocrat, but would give tribal leaders who'd walked 20 days across Afghanistan to see him 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常成功的大学教授和世界银行技术官僚，但只会给那些跋涉20天穿越阿富汗来见他的部落首领10分钟时间。

sentences.en: He'd literally say, you've got 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他会直截了当地说，你只有10分钟。

sentences.en: Another story I've heard, which is interesting, is that he also put his feet up in front of tribal elders.
sentences.zh: 我听到的另一个有趣的故事是，他还在部落长老面前把脚翘起来。

sentences.en: Now, in India still today, I've always been taught that you must never point your feet at someone.
sentences.zh: 在今天的印度，我一直被教导说，你绝不能用脚指着别人。

sentences.en: If you're sitting cross-legged, it's hugely rude in that culture to point your feet or to put your feet up.
sentences.zh: 如果你盘腿坐着，在那种文化中用脚指着别人或把脚翘起来是非常粗鲁的。

sentences.en: Ashraf Ghani had a sort of poof in front of his armchair, and he'd just put his feet up like you would at home.
sentences.zh: 阿什拉夫·加尼的扶手椅前有一个脚凳，他就像在家里一样把脚翘在上面。

sentences.en: But this went down apparently very badly and serially offended a whole series of tribal elders who invited him to his inner sanctum.
sentences.zh: 但这显然产生了非常糟糕的影响，并连续冒犯了一系列邀请他进入其核心圈子的部落长老。

sentences.en: And Karzai never did this.
sentences.zh: 而卡尔扎伊从不这样做。

sentences.en: And a weird story with this is that Karzai read my book, Return of a King,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有一个奇怪的故事，卡尔扎伊读了我的书《国王归来》，

sentences.en: and he had always been haunted by the fact that Shashuja was his forebear and that Shashuja had died regarded as a traitor by many of the Afghans.
sentences.zh: 他一直被一个事实所困扰，即沙舒贾是他的祖先，而且沙舒贾死时被许多阿富汗人视为叛徒。

sentences.en: And he was particularly worried because the tribe which brought down Shashuja, who were the tribesmen of the man whose mistress, Alexander Burns, seduced, Abdullah Khan Achaqsa,
sentences.zh: 他特别担心，因为推翻沙舒贾的部落，也就是亚历山大·伯恩斯的情妇所诱惑的那个人的部落成员，阿卜杜拉·汗·阿查克扎伊，

sentences.en: were the Gilzai tribe.
sentences.zh: 是吉尔扎伊部落。

sentences.en: And the Gilzai, remarkably today, are the foot soldiers of the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 而吉尔扎伊人，值得注意的是，今天正是塔利班的步兵。

sentences.en: And so beneath what we perceive very easily today as a simple battle of Democrats and Westernized Afghans against Islamist tribal barbarians,
sentences.zh: 因此，在今天我们很容易将其视为民主人士和西方化的阿富汗人对抗伊斯兰部落野蛮人的简单战斗之下，

sentences.en: actually masks a old tribal fault line, which is the Barakzai's and Popolzai's, who are the Tophs, the landowners, against the Gilzai,
sentences.zh: 实际上掩盖了一个古老的部落断层线，即巴拉克扎伊和波帕尔扎伊，他们是地主，对抗吉尔扎伊，

sentences.en: who are the herdsmen and the day laborers on the Popolzai's land.
sentences.zh: 他们是波帕尔扎伊土地上的牧民和日工。

sentences.en: And Mullah Omar is a descendant of the resistance meter of 1842.
sentences.zh: 而毛拉·奥马尔是1842年抵抗运动领袖的后裔。

sentences.en: So really, the implication of all that, well, that would, for some listeners, they will say that that creates a sense of inevitability,
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切的含义，嗯，对于一些听众来说，他们会说这创造了一种必然感，

sentences.en: that the patterns of history are merely repeating themselves.
sentences.zh: 历史的模式只是在重复自己。

sentences.en: Is that too simplistic, though?
sentences.zh: 但这是否太简单化了？

sentences.en: Or do you think there is a kind of truth?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为有一种真理？

sentences.en: In this case, we did literally put the same guy on the throne twice.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们确实两次把同一个人推上了王位。

sentences.en: We put the head of the Popolzai tribe and he was brought down by the Gilzai.
sentences.zh: 我们扶持了波帕尔扎伊部落的首领，而他被吉尔扎伊人推翻了。

sentences.en: It was that simple.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: And as I say, the weird story that followed is that Karzai read Return of the King very closely.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，随之而来的奇怪故事是，卡尔扎伊非常仔细地阅读了《国王归来》。

sentences.en: He was given it by someone as he was on his way to Washington to meet Obama.
sentences.zh: 在他前往华盛顿会见奥巴马的路上，有人给了他这本书。

sentences.en: And none of us knew any about this until WikiLeaks, because it turned out that Hillary Clinton was very upset because when he came out of the place,
sentences.zh: 在维基解密之前，我们对此一无所知，因为事实证明希拉里·克林顿非常生气，因为当他从那个地方出来时，

sentences.en: having read this book, he altered his policy and began to be publicly much more hostile to the Americans, while taking their help, while taking their military.
sentences.zh: 读了这本书后，他改变了政策，开始在公开场合对美国人更加敌视，同时接受他们的帮助，接受他们的军事力量。

sentences.en: He saw it as vital that he didn't look like Shahshuja and appeared to be the puppet of the Americans.
sentences.zh: 他认为不让自己看起来像沙舒贾，不表现得像美国人的傀儡至关重要。

sentences.en: And so publicly started making very rude remarks about Americans, you know, creating casualties by inadequate intelligence, bombing the wrong villages, all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以公开开始发表关于美国人的非常粗鲁的言论，你知道，因为情报不足造成伤亡，轰炸错误的村庄，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And he was very frosty to Obama and WikiLeaks revealed these letters, emails from Hillary Clinton, which were, we now know, taken by the Russians and handed to WikiLeaks.
sentences.zh: 他对奥巴马非常冷淡，维基解密披露了这些来自希拉里·克林顿的信件和电子邮件，我们现在知道，这些是被俄国人窃取并交给维基解密的。

sentences.en: That what is this bloody book that Karzai is reading?
sentences.zh: 卡尔扎伊在读什么该死的书？

sentences.en: Ever since he's picked it up, he's become completely intransigent and won't talk to us.
sentences.zh: 自从他拿起这本书，他就变得完全不可妥协，不愿与我们交谈。

sentences.en: And this is incredibly rude.
sentences.zh: 这真是太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: And this was all on the, when WikiLeaks came out, this is all on the front page of the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 当维基解密发布时，这一切都在《纽约时报》的头版上。

sentences.en: And at this point, I then got invited to, to, to, to brief the, but the best bit was when Karzai then called me to, won Ramadan, to his palace, now occupied by the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，我被邀请去简报，但最好的是当卡尔扎伊在斋月期间叫我去他的宫殿，现在被塔利班占领了。

sentences.en: I saw a picture on the internet this morning of the Taliban flag flying over the Ard, the, the old citadel in the center of Kabul.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我在网上看到一张照片，塔利班旗帜在喀布尔市中心的旧城堡上空飘扬。

sentences.en: But we basically did a deal.
sentences.zh: 但我们基本上做了一笔交易。

sentences.en: And Karzai said, if you come to me during Ramadan, which is the kind of, you know, big fasting and the holiday in Islam as well,
sentences.zh: 卡尔扎伊说，如果你在斋月期间来找我，你知道，这是伊斯兰教中重要的斋戒和节日，

sentences.en: come to me during Ramadan and we will talk every evening after Iftar, after the breaking the faSt.
sentences.zh: 在斋月期间来找我，我们每天晚上在开斋后谈话。

sentences.en: We will have fruit together and I will ask you about Shashuja.
sentences.zh: 我们一起吃点水果，我会问你关于沙舒贾的事。

sentences.en: And in return, you can have an interview.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，你可以对我进行采访。

sentences.en: So I got six hours of interview with Karzai, which went into a, a New York Times profile, which is online if anyone wants to read it.
sentences.zh: 所以我得到了卡尔扎伊六个小时的采访，这些内容后来写进了《纽约时报》的一篇人物专访里，如果有人想读的话，网上有。

sentences.en: And in return, Karzai got to ask all the questions about Shashuja from these sources, which Ashraf Ghani had given me.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，卡尔扎伊得以从阿什拉夫·加尼提供给我的这些资料中，问了我所有关于沙舒贾的问题。

sentences.en: So it's all, it's a rare case of a history book in a small way, genuinely altering the course of, of policy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个罕见的例子，历史书在某种程度上真正改变了政策的走向。

sentences.en: In the end, of course, it didn't make any difference because as we now know, the, the wider lineaments of history repeating overtook all this.
sentences.zh: 当然，最终这并没有产生任何影响，因为正如我们现在所知，历史重演的更宏大的轮廓掩盖了这一切。

sentences.en: And we now have been back exactly where we were at the end of the 1842 First Anglo-Afghan War with the same ruler in charge.
sentences.zh: 我们现在又回到了1842年第一次英阿战争结束时的原点，由同一位统治者掌权。

sentences.en: Well, that's the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Isn't it, Willie?
sentences.zh: 不是吗，威利？

sentences.en: Do you think looking back now after 20 years, I mean, I know this is a massive question and we're reaching the end of the podcast anyway.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去20年，我知道这是一个宏大的问题，而且我们的播客也快结束了，你认为呢？

sentences.en: But do you think the Taliban's victory was inevitable?
sentences.zh: 你认为塔利班的胜利是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't think it was inevitable.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I think Karzai showed that with the right plightness and kindness and by distancing himself from his Western host,
sentences.zh: 我认为卡尔扎伊证明了，只要有适当的礼貌和善意，并与他的西方东道主保持距离，

sentences.en: he could mask the fact that he was kept in power by a Western puppet master and make a regime which was acceptable to the Afghans.
sentences.zh: 他就能掩盖自己被西方傀儡大师控制的事实，并建立一个阿富汗人可以接受的政权。

sentences.en: But it was touch and go.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是千钧一发。

sentences.en: And when someone less dexterous, Ashraf Ghani, took over and was rude to people and diminished the popularity of the,
sentences.zh: 当一个没那么圆滑的人，阿什拉夫·加尼接手后，他对人粗鲁，削弱了政权的受欢迎程度，

sentences.en: of the regime and alienated one by one tribal leaders from across the country.
sentences.zh: 并疏远了全国各地的部落首领。

sentences.en: Ashraf actually, you know, had a temper.
sentences.zh: 阿什拉夫其实，你知道，脾气很暴躁。

sentences.en: He used to throw things at people.
sentences.zh: 他过去常向人扔东西。

sentences.en: I heard a story, for example, one press conference where he threw an ashtray at a female journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我听说过一个故事，例如，在一次新闻发布会上，他向一位女记者扔了烟灰缸。

sentences.en: So that sort of thing just doesn't play.
sentences.zh: 所以那种行为是行不通的。

sentences.en: Because, Willie, I mean, the general sense that historians have is the interplay of great tectonic plates grinding against each other, vast impersonal forces.
sentences.zh: 因为，威利，历史学家普遍认为，历史是巨大的构造板块相互挤压的结果，是巨大的非个人力量。

sentences.en: But in 1842, it's Burns seducing the wrong woman.
sentences.zh: 但在1842年，是因为伯恩斯勾引了错误的女人。

sentences.en: And you're saying that now it's, you know, it's a guy throwing ashtrays at people.
sentences.zh: 而你现在说，是因为一个向人扔烟灰缸的家伙。

sentences.en: I think we know in our own time.
sentences.zh: 我想我们自己时代的人都清楚。

sentences.en: Are those those tiny kind of trigger points that that affect?
sentences.zh: 那些微小的触发点会产生影响吗？

sentences.en: I think from our own experience, in our own time, there are tiny things that these great forces of history, these great Tolstoyan moments,
sentences.zh: 我认为根据我们自己的经验，在我们这个时代，确实存在一些微小的事情，这些伟大的历史力量，这些伟大的托尔斯泰式的时刻，

sentences.en: these great Tolstoyan forces which form the economy and shape the destination do exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这些塑造经济和决定命运的伟大的托尔斯泰式的力量是存在的。

sentences.en: But equally, tiny little accidents can alter things.
sentences.zh: 但同样，微小的意外也能改变事情。

sentences.en: For example, in our own time, if Boris Johnson had had, you know, he famously wrote the two articles pro-Brexit and against Brexit.
sentences.zh: 例如，在我们这个时代，如果鲍里斯·约翰逊，你知道，他曾写过两篇著名的文章，一篇支持脱欧，一篇反对脱欧。

sentences.en: If he had actually decided to back camera and not taken the part of going for Brexit, would we be where we are now with Europe?
sentences.zh: 如果他当时真的决定支持卡梅伦，而不是选择支持脱欧，我们现在还会处于欧洲的这种境地吗？

sentences.en: Quite possibly not.
sentences.zh: 很可能不会。

sentences.en: One man's decision at a crucial moment can alter things.
sentences.zh: 一个人在关键时刻的决定可以改变事情。

sentences.en: In the context of Afghanistan, though, you say that this is a society where politeness is very important and knowing the rules of courtesy are very important.
sentences.zh: 不过，在阿富汗的背景下，你说这是一个礼貌非常重要、了解礼节规则非常重要的社会。

sentences.en: Do you think it's a problem for the West right the way from the 1840s that we tend not to know these rules?
sentences.zh: 你认为从1840年代开始，西方往往不了解这些规则是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: It certainly is a problem.
sentences.zh: 这当然是个问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, as I said, there are a huge array of possibilities every day in all our lives.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，正如我所说，我们每个人的生活中每天都有无数的可能性。

sentences.en: If we were to turn right rather than to turn left at a given moment, how history would be different.
sentences.zh: 如果我们当时向右转而不是向左转，历史会变得多么不同。

sentences.en: But, yes, I think I don't think that it was impossible that a pro-Western regime could have survived in Afghanistan because the Taliban were very unpopular.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我不认为亲西方政权在阿富汗生存是不可能的，因为塔利班非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: They were an extremely brutal regime.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个极其残暴的政权。

sentences.en: This regime now, though, is regarded as incredibly corrupt.
sentences.zh: 不过，现在的这个政权被认为极其腐败。

sentences.en: And it's rather like the Islamic revolution in Iran in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 这有点像70年代伊朗的伊斯兰革命。

sentences.en: There is a huge number of people who feel that a small elite have gobbled up corruptly huge sums of money.
sentences.zh: 有大量的人认为一小部分精英腐败地吞噬了巨额资金。

sentences.en: There are stories circulating in Kabul now that Ashraf Ghani's car was stuffed with cash and they couldn't get it all in the plane he escaped in.
sentences.zh: 现在喀布尔流传着这样的故事：阿什拉夫·加尼的车里塞满了现金，他们无法把钱全部装进他逃跑时乘坐的飞机里。

sentences.en: And a lot of the money was left on the runway in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 很多钱被留在了喀布尔的跑道上。

sentences.en: Three or four people have told me the story.
sentences.zh: 有三四个人跟我讲过这个故事。

sentences.en: I have no idea whether it's true or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是真是假。

sentences.en: But the fact that enough people believe these stories creates an atmosphere where the regime that has just ended was seen to be corrupt, greedy.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，足够多的人相信这些故事，创造了一种氛围，使得刚刚结束的政权被视为腐败、贪婪。

sentences.en: Ghani's nephew left in a Learjet with an Instagram post saying trying to leave.
sentences.zh: 加尼的侄子坐着私人飞机离开了，并在Instagram上发帖说正在尝试离开。

sentences.en: Yeah, I saw that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我看到了。

sentences.en: That sort of thing creates massive upset with poor people who have not got their hands in the money pot, who are not eating the honey.
sentences.zh: 那种事情会让那些没有接触到钱袋、没有吃到蜂蜜的穷人感到极度愤怒。

sentences.en: And I think many people will be waiting to see whether this regime is better for them.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人会拭目以待，看看这个政权是否对他们更好。

sentences.en: Many women will have their lives destroyed.
sentences.zh: 许多女性的生活将被摧毁。

sentences.en: There will be huge cruelty.
sentences.zh: 会有巨大的残忍。

sentences.en: There will be terrible.
sentences.zh: 会有可怕的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I personally think it's a catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我个人认为这是一场灾难。

sentences.en: And I have many, many friends whose lives have been hobbled and restricted and whose lives may well be in danger.
sentences.zh: 我有很多很多朋友，他们的生活受到了阻碍和限制，他们的生命很可能处于危险之中。

sentences.en: I got an email from Karzai's office this morning saying he's OK and that he's read rather like, in fact,
sentences.zh: 今天早上我收到卡尔扎伊办公室的一封邮件，说他很好，而且他读起来，事实上，

sentences.en: to kind of carry on up the Kaiba email saying there was some moments of tension, but all is now restored.
sentences.zh: 有点像《凯伯山口》里的情节，说虽然有几刻紧张，但一切现在都恢复了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What a somber note in which to end.
sentences.zh: 这是一个多么沉重的结尾。

sentences.en: Incredible sang-froid.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的冷静。

sentences.en: But, you know, many people's lives will be deeply damaged by this.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，许多人的生活将因此受到深刻的伤害。

sentences.en: Whether this regime manages to solidify itself and hold together like Dos Mohamed managed after the catastrophe of 1842 when he came back into power remains to be seen.
sentences.zh: 这个政权是否能像多斯特·穆罕默德在1842年灾难后重掌权力那样巩固自身并保持团结，还有待观察。

sentences.en: Already, certainly, the Taliban have proved to be far more disciplined and less fractured than we all thought they were.
sentences.zh: 当然，塔利班已经证明他们比我们所有人想象的要纪律严明得多，分裂也少得多。

sentences.en: The idea was that there was a bunch of disparate hooligans and fundamentalists in the hills, incapable, really, of cohering and managing a coordinated campaign.
sentences.zh: 人们的想法是，山里有一群分散的流氓和原教旨主义者，实际上无法团结起来并进行协调一致的行动。

sentences.en: But that was clearly very wrong.
sentences.zh: 但那显然是非常错误的。

sentences.en: It's been an extraordinary military success.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非凡的军事成功。

sentences.en: So a bit like the way that the various tribes in 1842 got together to absolutely seal the doom of the British retreat.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像1842年各部落联合起来彻底封锁英军撤退之路的方式。

sentences.en: Exactly that.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Although, again, you know, there were all sorts of tensions and tribal rivalries within the resistance of the British.
sentences.zh: 虽然，再次强调，你知道，在反抗英国人的过程中，存在着各种各样的紧张局势和部落竞争。

sentences.en: But they held together.
sentences.zh: 但他们团结在一起了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that's an incredibly somber note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个极其沉重的结尾。

sentences.en: And again, absolute tour de force of historical explication.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢，绝对是历史阐释的杰作。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，威利。

sentences.en: Thank you.

sentences.zh: 你保持了你的记录。

sentences.zh: 是的，你绝对可以保持你的记录。

sentences.zh: 还有一件事，我想以另一个话题结束，这与阿富汗无关，但与伊拉克有关，

sentences.en: where Western forces also intervened and left a kind of a lot of damage.
sentences.zh: 西方军队也在那里进行了干预，并留下了很多破坏。

sentences.en: And it's a walk that I'm doing on the 23rd and 24th.
sentences.zh: 这是我将在23日和24日进行的一次徒步活动。

sentences.en: So that's next Monday, if you're listening to this as it comes out.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在节目发布时收听，那就是下周一。

sentences.en: And next Tuesday, walking 50 miles in 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 还有下周二，24小时内步行50英里。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
